recreation_brief:
1. Create a blank PowerPoint slide with white background.
2. Draw a vertical blue divider line around 35% from the left edge.
3. On the left side, stack four red-bordered panels vertically. In each panel: add a red header box with 'Threshold=0.0', 'Threshold=0.1', 'Threshold=0.3', and 'Threshold=0.4' respectively. Below each header, insert a 2x2 table with header row 'Predicted as | P | N' and row headers 'Actual P' and 'Actual N'. Fill cells as follows: Threshold 0.0: P row 5,0; N row 6,0. Threshold 0.1: P row 5,0; N row 4,2. Threshold 0.3: P row 5,0; N row 2,4. Threshold 0.4: P row 4,1; N row 1,5. To the right of each table, add the TPR and FPR equations exactly as transcribed.
4. In the center strip, leave blank white space and optionally add a mouse cursor arrow.
5. On the right side, create a panel with light gray background. At the top, draw an ROC plot: light cyan plot area, y-axis 'TPR', x-axis 'FPR', grid lines, four red dots with white labels '0.3', '0.1', '0.0', '0.4' at approximate positions, axis arrows. Add a yellow circle with '32' at the top-right corner of this panel.
6. At the bottom-right, add a light blue box with 'TPR = TP / (TP + FN)' and 'FPR = FP / (FP + TN)'. Next to it, add a small confusion matrix with green TP and TN cells, red FP and FN cells, labeled 'Predicted as | P | N' with rows 'Actual P' and 'Actual N'.
7. Use black sans-serif text for all labels and values.
